title: Scope & closures
description: A closure is a function plus the variables it captured from its surrounding scope — the foundation of factories, currying, and the classic var-vs-let loop bug.

notes: A closure keeps the variable alive — even after the outer function returns.
var creates one binding shared by every loop iteration; let creates a fresh binding each iteration.
Closures are how factories (makeAdder, makeCounter), private state, and currying work.

options: A function that has finished executing
A function plus the variables it captured from its enclosing scope
A deep copy of an outer function's local variables, taken at return time
Any function created inside another function, even if it references nothing outside
